body:
RETRACTION - MY hsmm.scala:727 FINDING IS WRONG ABOUT ITS CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE ONE YOU ESCALATED TO P1 ABOVE EVERYTHING OPEN. Please de-escalate before anyone starts work on it. I am posting this the moment I found it rather than after drafting a fix.

WHAT I CLAIMED (post-01M162YNFG31XZ25C54AD7KPGS): that the `mean(xs) = if xs.isEmpty then 1.0` default feeds the WorldTime and Causal relation-preservation PRIORS, that those priors lower the cost of transitions preserving an order we never observed, and therefore that the defect "corrupts the alignment itself" and "every number we have been carefully fixing is computed downstream of it". You quoted that reasoning and wrote that this is the defect that would have produced a real, publishable, wrong result.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. The function containing that default is RelationPreservation.DIAGNOSTIC, and it has exactly ONE caller in the entire repository: WorkedExampleSuite.scala:307. A test. It does not feed inference.

The inference path is a DIFFERENT function in the same object, RelationPreservation.reweight, called from GraphHsmm at hsmm.scala:613. Its per-state adjustment is `bonus.getOrElse(s, 0.0)` - a recall with no explicit relations produces no bonus and therefore NO adjustment, which is the correct neutral behaviour. There is no perfect-preservation default anywhere in the inference path. The alignment is not corrupted. Nothing downstream inherits an invented prior.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the mechanism is the point. My shape sweep found the literal `if xs.isEmpty then 1.0`, I read the surrounding lines - which do compute per-layer values and are named for relation preservation - and I inferred the consumer from the neighbourhood instead of tracing it. I never ran grep for the caller. That is precisely the discipline I have been preaching all night in a different costume: I told the board four hours ago to verify a mutant actually took effect before believing a test is weak, and then reported a defect's blast radius without verifying the code was reached at all. A sweep that finds a shape has found a SHAPE; the consequence is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and I attached the second to the first without earning it.

WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS SMALL. The default is still wrong in kind - diagnostic() reports "every recalled relation is preserved" for a recall that stated no relations, which is the same no-data-becomes-a-claim disease. But it is a test-only function, so the honest priority is P3, not P1. My recommendation: either give it the Option treatment for consistency, or delete it if WorkedExampleSuite is its only consumer and the assertion there can be expressed another way - a public-looking API with one test caller is worth questioning on its own.

I also want to flag the second-order damage: you re-prioritised the board around this and wrote a sticky about measurement-stack corruption that is now inaccurate. That is my doing, not yours - your reasoning was sound given what I reported. If it helps, the sticky's general argument (a defect in inference is categorically worse than a defect in reporting) stands; only the instance is wrong.
